pr_title: Fix tooltip appearing in old place, on movement
pr_body:
Fixes #96707

Also fixes tooltip appearing even if mouse is in steady motion (now accepts max 5 px movement).
![tooltip2](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/55f770ec-6c83-4399-8216-7c9eca7de09d)

issue_context.title: Tooltip sometimes appears at old mouse position
issue_context.body:
### Tested versions

4.4 dev 5675c76
Not reproducible in 4.3

### System information

Windows 10.0.19045 - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1060 (NVIDIA; 31.0.15.4633) - Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-7700HQ CPU @ 2.80GHz (8 Threads)

### Issue description

If you move cursor before hovering over something with tooltip, the tooltip can appear at older mouse position.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/27982e1e-b547-422b-a14b-cae7c34d26c1



### Steps to reproduce

1. Hover scene tree node while moving your cursor fast

comments:
It seems to me that this bit has a little logic problem:
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/5675c76461e197d3929a1142cfb84ab1a76ac9dd/scene/main/viewport.cpp#L1936-L1941
The intent is that if the mouse has moved 5 pixels reset the tooltip timer. However, `mm->get_relative()` gets the relative motion to the last inputevent, not in relation to where the timer was started. So it means like 5 pixels per frame (or however often inputevent are triggered).
So the bug is a bit more severe, tooltip appears even if the mouse is in steady motion.
![tooltip](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/166e2ce2-6062-4f89-a3ab-1e3d87c56dd2)

I think solution to this would be either use the initial version of #95846 (check that relative motion != zero), or if we really want that 5 px leeway, save the starting position. But I think zero movement is good enough, the situation is different from doubleclicking, since to show tooltip you can just not touch the mouse (vs accessibility problem of doubleclicking without moving mouse).

Edit: After testing the first solution I mentioned, it seems to fix the problem I found but not the original issue. I still think it's going to be one solution that fixes both of these, so I won't open a separate issue just yet.

Edit2: I tried implementing the second solution and it seems to work well. There wasn't even need to introduce a new property for tracking the position, I hijacked the existing `gui.tooltip_pos` 👌

review_comments: Am I missing something here or is this line unnecessary? The property gets overwritten anyways in few lines further so I removed this one.
I agree that this is unnecessary.

I don't think we want to remove the check for a stopped timer. The goal of the minimum distance test is to prevent the timer from from being reset by small mouse movements, _not_ to prevent the timer from being started in the first place. With the proposed change, a user may be confused by a tooltip not displaying just because they haven't moved their mouse enough. This could happen if their mouse had been sitting just a few pixels away from the control of interest before they moved to it.

Also, the proposed change no longer matches the comments describing the desired behavior above.

I see. I think checking for the stopped timer also doesn't resolve that problem. Eg. mouse is moved to near the control, then it's moved inside the control before the timer stops => no triggering.

I think the solution is to check if there's a new control under the mouse and restart the timer in that case.
Yes, we could reset the timer if `over` doesn't match `gui.tooltip_control`.
